newsitem.title: USA: Santa Anita terminates Colony agreement.
newsitem.headline: Santa Anita terminates Colony agreement.

text.p: The Santa Anita Cos said Tuesday its agreement with Colony Capital Inc to recapitalize Santa Anita has been terminated, resulting in a $4.5 million charge against first quarter earnings.

The two companies signed an agreement in August 1996 whereby real estate investment firm Colony would invest $138 million to recapitalize Santa Anita Cos over time in return for a 45 percent stake on a fully diluted basis.

On January 7, Santa Anita and Colony revised their agreement so that Santa Anita could enter into discussions and negotiations with third parties in light of an increase in Santa Anita's share price beyond the value of the proposed strategic alliance with Colony. When Santa Anita announced the deal last August its shares were traded at 13-5/8, on Tuesday its shares closed at 27-1/8 on the New York Stock Exchange.

Santa Anita said it paid Colony a $4 million break-up fee, plus expenses of $500,000. The payment of the break-up fee and related expenses will be charged against Santa Anita's 1997 first quarter earnings. In the year-ago quarter, the company reported a profit of $8.1 million, or $0.72 a share.
Santa Anita said it is in final negotiations with a select number of potential buyers.
